name: Load a round part into the ST-25's 3-jaw chuck, its end on the soft jaws' step, clamp it with the foot pedal; and take it out

working.role: carries the part into the open jaws and holds it on their step until they close; lifts it out after

steadying.role: rests at the side; the foot presses the pedal

phases.what: Door open, spindle stopped: the foot on the pedal opens the jaws if they're closed (each press toggles them) [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the jaws open, 2.2 mm clear of a part of their bore's size

phases.what: The working hand to the part where it waits, opening round its rim
Fingertips and thumb round the rim, the part's face toward the chuck; take its weight [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
Carry it through the door's opening to the chuck, its axis turned onto the spindle's, in front of the jaws [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the part on the spindle's axis, 10 mm in front of the jaws

phases.what: Slide it into the jaws' bore until its end meets their step, then a light push to seat it [proposed: force_n, travel_mm, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the part's end on the step

phases.what: Holding it there, the foot presses the pedal: the jaws close on it in about half a second [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the jaws gripping it at the job's pressure

phases.what: Let go and draw the hand back out of the door's opening [proposed: duration_s]
Look that it sits square on the step, no gap at its end [proposed: duration_s]
To unload, with the door open and the spindle stopped, the working hand to the part, round its rim
Hold it; the foot presses the pedal and the jaws open [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the part loose in the open jaws

phases.what: Draw it straight off the step out of the bore, then out of the door's opening to its place [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the part clear of the machine

sources.ref: Haas Automation, 2023 Lathe Operator's Manual: 1.2 (7. Foot Pedal), 3.2 chuck safety, 3.5 Run/Setup Mode Restrictions
sources.gives: chuck clamp and unclamp allowed with the door open; hydraulic pressure set to hold the part securely without distortion; jaws not beyond the chuck's diameter; part loading: open the door, do the task, close the door

sources.ref: Haas Automation, Foot Pedal - Troubleshooting Guide - NGC (TG0066), and the M10/M11 and Settings 282-284 pages
sources.gives: the foot pedal works the chuck's clamp and unclamp, its input toggling when pressed; M10 clamps, M11 unclamps; OD clamping closes the jaws toward the centre; no unclamp above Setting 283's rpm; no Cycle Start unclamped (284)

sources.ref: Haas Factory Outlet (Morris Trident TMT), Haas Lathe Set-up course: work holding, types of jaws
sources.gives: the hydraulic chuck worked by the foot pedal or M-codes; its pressure set for the operation (roughing up to 300-400 psi, finishing as little as 100 psi); the jaws' limited stroke; soft jaws bored to hold a diameter, for second operations, clamping without marking a turned surface and running concentric
jaw stroke 8.8 mm on the diameter; 123 kN of static grip at 49 kN of draw

sources.ref: Kurt, 'Double Station Manual Vise Setup' (YouTube), measured locally with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker; borrowed, as no lathe-loading footage was tracked
sources.gives: reach durations: the right hand's interquartile range, 0.32-0.67 s

notes: For ll-1007224's two setups in the Kitagawa's soft jaws, bored Ø63.5 and 8 mm deep to a step (moonshot/planning/plans/ll-1007224.json): op10's 1 in blank and op20's flipped part are loaded and unloaded so. The jaws are bored near mid-stroke, so open they stand 2.2 mm clear of a part of the bore's size all round and close on it 2.2 mm in (moonshot/library/stations/st25.json). With 8 mm of a 25.4 mm blank in the jaws its middle is outside them: unheld it tips out, so the hand holds it on the step until the jaws close (as moonshot/tests/gates/test_lathe_cell_conformance.py does). The foot on the pedal is an input to the control, not a simulated foot: the body model has no legs (station gap; Control.press_pedal), for the user's decision. Proposed, with reasons (phase numbers count from 1): one hand carries and holds the part, as a 0.2 kg disc needs, the other free; the disc's grasp by its rim, its face toward the chuck, so the fingers stay out of the bore; #1, #6 and #10 the pedal's 0.5-0.6 s (the jaws close their 2.2 mm in about 0.4 s at 10 kN of draw, the station's oil damping); #3 4 N and 0.5 s to take a 0.2 kg blank's weight with margin; #4 and #11 1.5-2.5 s through the opening; #5 10 N and 10 mm to seat it, as a light push home; #7 0.8 s; #8 1.5 s. The job's pressure is the plan's: the station's default draw is 10 kN, about 100 psi, a finishing pressure.
